title: JavaScript Classes Core Check
description: Check your understanding of class syntax, constructors, instance methods, inheritance, static methods, getters, setters, and fields.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is a class in JavaScript?

options.text: A blueprint for creating objects with shared structure and behavior
A special kind of array method
A variable that cannot be changed

questions.explanation: A class defines a blueprint for creating instances with shared behavior and per-instance data.

questions.prompt: Which keyword creates an instance of a class?
questions.explanation: Use `new ClassName(...)` to create an instance of a class.

options.text: It runs when a new instance is created and initializes instance data
It always creates a static method

questions.explanation: The constructor runs during `new ClassName(...)` and usually initializes instance properties.

questions.prompt: Inside a constructor called with `new`, what does `this` refer to?
questions.explanation: When a class is called with `new`, `this` inside the constructor refers to the new object.

questions.prompt: Which syntax defines an instance method?
questions.explanation: Class instance methods use method shorthand syntax inside the class body.

options.text: Creates a child class that inherits from a parent class

questions.explanation: `extends` creates an inheritance relationship between a child class and a parent class.

questions.prompt: What must a derived class constructor call before using `this`?
questions.explanation: A child class constructor must call `super()` before accessing `this`.

questions.prompt: How do you call a static method named `createGuest` on class `User`?
questions.explanation: Static methods belong to the class itself, so they are called on the class.
Getters are methods that are read like properties, such as `user.fullName`.

questions.prompt: What symbol starts a private class field?
Which relationship is best modeled with inheritance?
questions.explanation: Inheritance is best for true `is-a` relationships, such as `Admin is a User`.

questions.prompt: Which relationship is usually better modeled with composition?
questions.explanation: Composition is often better for `has-a` relationships, such as a car having an engine.
